# Repo-Size Cleanup — Measurements & Coordinated History-Rewrite Spec

_Status: draft for team review. The no-coordination half is **already committed**
on `chore/repo-size-cleanup` (commit `95010d3`). The history rewrite below
requires team sign-off because it rewrites every commit SHA._

---

## 1. Measured ground truth

Taken from a full (non-shallow) local clone — 3,880 commits, 601 refs after a
stale-ref prune. Numbers come from a full-history blob inventory
(`git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file --batch-check`), not estimates.

### On-disk `.git` (1.2 GB before, ~1.1 GB after local reclaim)

| Component | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pack (`.git/objects/pack`) | **308 MB** | All commit history. ~266 MB is deleted-file "ghosts". |
| LFS local cache (`.git/lfs`) | **771 MB** | Current + recent baselines. Was 875 MB; `git lfs prune` freed ~104 MB. |

A **fresh clone** transfers roughly: **308 MB pack + ~339 MB LFS-at-HEAD ≈ ~650 MB**.
That is the ~500 MB+ people observe (more, depending on LFS history fetched).

### History weight: ghost vs live

Summing the largest blob per unique path across all history:

- **Live (still at HEAD): 108 MB**
- **Ghost (deleted from HEAD, pure dead weight): 266 MB**

Top ghost prefixes — these no longer exist in the working tree and are 100% safe
to purge from history:

| Ghost weight | Path prefix | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| 135.9 MB | `packages/producer/**` | Untracked failure frames (26.5 MB / 146 revs), **nested raw HDR-regression MP4s** that dodged the old non-recursive LFS globs, superseded `compiled.html` revisions, deleted fixtures |
| 56.3 MB | `docs/images/**` | Deleted catalog-preview MP4s/PNGs |
| 17.9 MB | `registry/blocks/**` | Superseded block assets (incl. the 42 MB of duplicate 5K backgrounds this branch just recompressed) |
| 9.8 MB | `qa-artifacts/**` | Scratch QA capture dir |
| 9.8 MB | `my-video/**` | Accidentally committed scratch render + TTS mp3 |
| 7.3 MB | `videos/**` | Scratch launch-video working dir |
| 5.5 MB | `evals/editframe/**` | Deleted eval artifacts |
| ~11 MB | deleted `skills/**` | Demo media from removed skill dirs |

### Churn on _live_ files (worth collapsing even though the file still exists)

- **`compiled.html` baselines: 48.3 MB across 131 blob-revisions** — only ~9 MB
  exists at HEAD; the other ~39 MB is superseded revisions. These are base64,
  so git can't delta them — every regeneration stores a full ~3 MB fresh copy.

### Raw video in history

- **156.8 MB across 31 raw (non-LFS) video blobs** — pre-LFS commits and the
  nested HDR MP4s. (LFS-tracked videos are ~130-byte pointers in the pack, so
  this number is purely the binaries that bypassed LFS.)

---

## 2. Already done (no coordination — committed on `chore/repo-size-cleanup`)

These shrink the **checkout** and **stop new growth**; they do not touch history.

1. **Untracked 158 failure-frame artifacts (~27 MB)** — generated debugging
   frames already covered by `.gitignore` but committed before the rule. `git rm
   --cached` (disk copies kept).
2. **Recompressed 13 identical block backgrounds** — 5120×2880 / 3.3 MB → 2560×1440
   q78 / ~428 KB each. **42 MB → 5.4 MB** in the tree. Kept per-block files so
   blocks stay portable on `hyperframes add`.
3. **Recursive LFS patterns** in `.gitattributes`
   (`packages/producer/tests/**/*.{mp4,mov,webm,png}`) — closes the leak that let
   nested HDR MP4s into the pack. Globalized `*.onnx`.
4. **`scripts/check-large-files.sh` + lefthook `largefiles` gate** — any staged
   file > 500 KB not routed through LFS fails the commit (excludes `registry/`).

### Local-only reclaim anyone can run today (no repo change)

```sh
git lfs prune                 # ~100 MB off .git/lfs
git remote prune origin       # drop stale remote-tracking refs
git gc --prune=now            # repack
```

### Clone-time relief for new clones (no repo change)

```sh
git clone --filter=blob:none <url>      # lazy-fetch old blobs
git clone --depth=1 <url>               # skip history
GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone <url>   # skip ~339 MB LFS payload until needed
```

Document the last one in the README: contributors who never run producer
regression tests don't need the LFS baselines, saving ~339 MB per clone.

---

## 3. Coordinated history rewrite (the ~270 MB win)

**Effect:** purge the 266 MB of ghosts + collapse `compiled.html` churn →
pack ~308 MB → an estimated **~70–90 MB**. Combined with LFS slimming (§4), a
fresh clone drops from ~650 MB to well under ~150 MB.

**Cost:** rewrites every commit SHA. Everyone must re-clone; open PRs must be
recreated/rebased; tags re-point. Do it once, announced, on a quiet window.

### Prerequisites

```sh
brew install git-filter-repo   # not installed locally yet
# or: pipx install git-filter-repo
```

### Step 0 — Freeze & back up

1. Announce a merge freeze; merge or note all open PRs (they will need re-basing).
2. Make a dated backup mirror you can roll back to:
   ```sh
   git clone --mirror git@github.com:heygen-com/hyperframes.git hyperframes-backup-YYYYMMDD.git
   ```
3. Confirm the backup has refs + LFS: `git -C hyperframes-backup-*.git lfs fetch --all`.

### Step 1 — Fresh mirror to operate on

```sh
git clone --mirror git@github.com:heygen-com/hyperframes.git hyperframes-rewrite.git
cd hyperframes-rewrite.git
```

### Step 2 — Purge ghost paths

Create `paths-to-purge.txt`:

```
# Scratch / accidental working dirs — never belonged in the repo
my-video/
videos/
qa-artifacts/
evals/
# Deleted catalog-preview media
docs/images/
# Generated debugging frames (now also gitignored)
glob:packages/producer/tests/**/failures/**
```

Then:

```sh
git filter-repo --invert-paths --paths-from-file paths-to-purge.txt
```

For path-globs filter-repo wants explicit `glob:` entries (as above) or use
`--path-glob`. Verify nothing live was caught (see Step 5).

> **Note on `skills/**` and `registry/**`:** their _ghost_ bytes are removed
> automatically by the general pass only if the specific deleted files are
> listed. Most live skill/registry media is **current** (e.g. the 36.6 MB of
> demo MP4s in `skills/hyperframes-animation/examples/assets/` are at HEAD) and
> must NOT be path-purged — see §4 for those.

### Step 3 — Collapse `compiled.html` churn (optional, ~39 MB)

These are derived test baselines. Two options:

- **A (recommended):** stop committing them at all — regenerate + hash-compare in
  CI (the Docker test path already does this for MP4s), and `--invert-paths` them
  out of history entirely.
- **B:** keep only the HEAD revision — strip historical revisions via
  `filter-repo --blob-callback` dropping `compiled.html` blobs not reachable
  from HEAD. (More fiddly; A is cleaner.)

If A: add `glob:packages/producer/tests/**/output/compiled.html` to
`paths-to-purge.txt` and add the path to `.gitignore`, plus a CI regen+compare step.

### Step 4 — Re-pack & push

```sh
git reflog expire --expire=now --all
git gc --prune=now --aggressive
# sanity-check size before pushing
du -sh .git
git push --force --mirror git@github.com:heygen-com/hyperframes.git
```

Then on the server / GitHub side, run `git lfs prune` semantics by re-pushing LFS
and asking GitHub support (or using the LFS API) to garbage-collect orphaned LFS
objects if you also slim baselines (§4).

### Step 5 — Verify

```sh
# No purged path survives anywhere in history:
git rev-list --objects --all | grep -E '^.* (my-video/|videos/|qa-artifacts/|evals/|docs/images/)' | head
# Pack size sanity:
git count-objects -vH | grep size-pack
# HEAD tree intact (build + tests still green):
bun install && bun run build && bun run test
```

### Step 6 — Team migration

- Announce SHAs changed. Everyone: `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/main` on
  clean branches, or simplest — **delete and re-clone**.
- Recreate open PRs from backup branches (cherry-pick onto rewritten `main`).
- Update any CI caches / submodule pins keyed on SHAs.

---

## 4. LFS baseline slimming (the other ~339 MB — coordinated, separate)

The pack rewrite does **not** shrink the LFS payload a clone fetches. Levers:

1. **Cap baseline size.** The worst golden baseline is `dogs-captions/output.mp4`
   at 54.5 MB; several are 10–27 MB. PSNR/SSIM checkpoint comparison does not need
   full-bitrate masters — re-encode baselines at a quantized CRF / shorter
   duration, target ≤5 MB each. Regenerate, commit as LFS, then GC old LFS objects.
2. **Default to skip-smudge.** Document `GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone`; have CI
   explicitly `git lfs pull` only in the producer-regression job. Most contributors
   never need the baselines → ~339 MB saved per clone immediately, zero rewrite.
3. **Decide the `*.wav` / raw-audio policy.** Deliberately left out of the
   `.gitattributes` LFS globalization on `chore/repo-size-cleanup` because
   `registry/` ships raw audio for block portability. If audio masters should be
   LFS outside registry, add a scoped pattern (and exclude `registry/`).

---

## 5. Recommended sequence

1. **Now, no coordination:** merge `chore/repo-size-cleanup`; document the
   skip-smudge / partial-clone options in the README; everyone runs the local
   `lfs prune` + `gc`.  ← shrinks checkout, stops growth, ~120 MB local relief.
2. **Next, low-risk coordinated:** slim LFS baselines (§4.1) + default skip-smudge
   (§4.2). Biggest clone-transfer win without a SHA rewrite.
3. **Finally, one-time coordinated rewrite (§3):** purge 266 MB of ghosts +
   collapse `compiled.html`. Schedule on a freeze window; everyone re-clones.

Estimated end state: **~650 MB clone → under ~150 MB.**

## Generalizability fix pushed (52d1947)

Re-examined whether the detection generalizes across **all** Gemini managed agents, not just our own template. It did **not**, as originally written.

**Finding:** the detector keyed on `existsSync('/.agents/AGENTS.md')`, but Google's Managed Agents docs are explicit that **AGENTS.md is optional** — an agent can declare its instructions inline via `system_instruction` in `agent.yaml` and ship no AGENTS.md file ("the `system_instruction` and `AGENTS.md` are additive; both apply when present"). The platform auto-discovers the agent under the **`/.agents/` directory**; skills mount at `/.agents/skills/`, workspace at `/workspace/`, and `AGENTS.md` at `/.agents/AGENTS.md` *only when shipped*.

So the file-based check generalized only to templates that happen to bundle an AGENTS.md — like our own `hyperframes-gemini-agent` and Thor's reference. A managed agent defined with inline instructions, or a skills-only definition, was a **silent false-negative**. All three verification spins used our AGENTS.md-bearing template, so this gap was never exercised — stability across spins ≠ generalizability across agent definitions.

**Fix:** key on the `/.agents/` directory mount instead of the AGENTS.md file. Still gVisor-guarded, so the false-positive surface is unchanged (`/.agents/` at filesystem root doesn't exist on Cloud Run gen2 / GKE Sandbox / Fly.io). Added a regression test for the skills-but-no-AGENTS.md case.

**Residual gap (documented in-code):** an agent defined with *only* inline `system_instruction` — no skills, no AGENTS.md — may not materialize a `/.agents/` mount at all. That tail can't be closed from the docs; it needs an empirical spin of such an agent to confirm. The common case (skills and/or AGENTS.md present) is now covered.

Sources: [Building Managed Agents](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/custom-agents), [Managed Agents Quickstart](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/managed-agents-quickstart).

Added a producer-level regression test: **`packages/producer/tests/webgl-video-texture-render-compat/`** (commit 47345ef).

It's a render-compat fixture — a WebGL2 canvas that samples a `<video>` as a texture on every `hf-seek` (the natural author pattern, distilled from the HeyGen prism into one small clip). The harness renders it through the full producer pipeline and compares against the golden:

- **With the fix** → the render reproduces the decoded video frames (visual PASS, 0 failed frames).
- **Without the fix** → the WebGL canvas renders black, so render-vs-golden PSNR collapses and the test fails.

I verified the golden actually contains real, time-varying video content (not black), so a regression is caught rather than passing vacuously. Kept it tiny (132 KB clip, 2 s @ 1280×720, 1 worker) so it's cheap in CI.

**Design / acknowledged:**

- **SDK session freshness vs originalContent** — the SDK session is opened from the same content as the server at session-creation time. The only way they diverge is if an external save lands while the session is open — which the reload-on-change hook in #1449 handles (hf:file-change fires → reloadToken increments → session re-opens). The 2000ms suppression only applies to self-write events (via `domEditSaveTimestampRef`), not external saves. So the session is always fresh relative to `originalContent` unless an external save is in-flight when `sdkCutoverPersist` runs — a race that's inherent to the optimistic-write pattern and not worth adding a content-hash crosscheck for.
- **Undo after cutover** — `domEditSaveTimestampRef` is set by `sdkCutoverPersist`, not by undo. So the undo path does NOT suppress the `hf:file-change` event. - **GSAP ops throw = breaking change / CHANGELOG** — this API (GSAP ops throwing instead of returning `EMPTY`) is not yet in any published release of `@hyperframes/sdk`. Will add a CHANGELOG entry before the release version that ships this stack. There are no external consumers of the pre-throw API surface to notify.
- **2000ms suppression path-awareness** — path-awareness is unnecessary by construction: `useSdkSession` is keyed on `(projectId, activeCompPath)`. When `activeCompPath` changes, the effect re-runs, a new session opens, and a fresh `domEditSaveTimestampRef` governs suppression for the new path. Cross-path contamination is structurally impossible.
- **sdkSessionRef mid-dispatch swap** — `sdkCutoverPersist` captures `sdkSession` as a parameter (value at call time), not by ref. The `sdkSessionRef.current` assignment in `useDomEditSession` can race during the `await writeProjectFile(...)` gap, but the in-progress dispatch closure holds the original session. Safe.
- **SELF_WRITE_SUPPRESS_MS configurable** — acknowledged for CI/slow-network cases. Can be made configurable via an env var if it becomes a flakiness source; not doing it speculatively.

Thanks @hobostay — this surfaced a genuinely unguarded route, so I've addressed it in #1477 and am closing this in favor of that.

What I found verifying against current `main`:
- The literal `../` LFI as described isn't reachable over HTTP — Hono's WHATWG URL layer normalizes `../` and decodes+collapses `%2e%2e` before routing, and `c.req.path` isn't otherwise percent-decoded. I ran a payload battery (`../`, `%2e%2e`, `%252e`, `..%2f`, `..\`, `/abs`) and all 404'd without leaking.
- But a **symlink** inside `rendersDir` pointing outside it *was* followed and served verbatim (verified: leaked an external secret, `200 OK`).

#1477 routes the filename through the existing `resolveWithinProject` chokepoint — the same helper the `composition` field on this route and `files.ts` already use. That closes the symlink escape and makes the route's safety independent of the URL layer's normalization. I went with the shared helper rather than the `filename.includes("..")` + `startsWith` check proposed here, because the string check is symlink-unsafe and would also reject legitimate filenames containing a `..` substring. Credited you in the PR description.

I reproduced the behavior (visible at t=14s, blank at t=20s+ with a child `data-duration="15"` under a 331s host), but after tracing it I don't think this is a runtime bug — it's working as designed, and it's a different case from #911.

**The distinction from #911:**

- **#911** was a child whose *internal GSAP timeline* (1s) was shorter than its *slot* (`data-duration=3`). The slot outlived the animation and went black. #917 fixed that by holding the child's final frame through its own `data-duration`. ✅
- **#1540** is a child whose *own `data-duration`* (15) is shorter than the host (331). Here there's nothing to "hold through" — the clip's window is simply over at 15s.

The rule you quoted — "`data-duration` takes precedence" — is exactly what's producing this: a clip with `data-duration="15"` is a 15-second window on the timeline and ends at 15s. Holding it to the host's 331s would require *ignoring* `data-duration`, i.e. the opposite of that rule, and would re-break the #917 contract (a correctly-sized slot must end on time even when its GSAP timeline is shorter). Your helmdeck workaround — rewriting the child `data-duration` to match the root — is actually the correct authoring fix: if you want a sub-composition to fill the whole host, its `data-duration` should span the host window.

That said, you're right that it fails **silently**, and a single full-bleed sub-composition shorter than its host is almost always a mistake. So rather than change the runtime, #1542 surfaces it at author time:

- A new lint rule, `subcomposition_blanks_before_host`, that warns when a sole/dominant sub-composition mount starting at ~0 ends before the host window (with a fixHint suggesting either extending `data-duration` or covering the tail). It's deliberately narrow so it stays quiet on intentional short clips like a 15s intro followed by another clip.
- A docs clarification in the sub-compositions reference calling out the shorter-than-host case explicitly, alongside the #911/#917 hold-through-slot behavior — which is the documentation gap your "Possible fixes → Docs" note flagged.

A spike in PostHog now tells you "raise `HF_STATIC_DEDUP_SAMPLES`" rather than "compositions are non-static."

**Bonus — retry double-count (found while re-reviewing):** the worker-perf push sat inside the adaptive-retry loop in `executeDiskCaptureWithAdaptiveRetry`, so a retry counted frames twice and could push `reused`/`predicted` past `totalFrames`. Now resets per attempt (retry replaces; no-retry path unchanged). Also: opt-out parsing now accepts `{false,0,off}` case-insensitively, `dedupPerfs` made required (was silently droppable), and the duplicated push loop extracted to `pushWorkerDedupPerfs` (which also drops `runCaptureStreamingStage` back under the complexity threshold).

Thanks @vanceingalls — and for the end-to-end lifecycle trace. On the two net-new notes:

**1. `ownsElement` O(N×M) per tick.** Agreed it's a non-issue at realistic audio
counts, and I'd rather not add it now. It mirrors the `setElementVolume`
`_activeSources.some(s => s.el === el)` already in the file, and a parallel
`WeakSet` mirror is duplicate state that has to stay in lockstep with
`_activeSources` across schedule-push / ended-splice / `stopAll` — that sync
surface is a more likely bug source than the O(N×M) scan is a perf problem for a
handful of tracks. Happy to switch to the WeakSet if a genuinely high-track-count
composition (dozens of overlapping audio clips) ever shows up in telemetry.

**2. HTMLMedia → transport handoff.** Two parts:

- *No sustained doubling* — provable from the code, not just the timing test:
  `el.muted = true` runs **synchronously** in the same `schedulePlayback`
  execution, immediately after `startBoundedSource` (the buffer `start()`) and
  before the source is pushed to `_activeSources`. So the element is silenced as
  the transport source begins — there's no async window where both produce
  audible output.
- *Alignment* — the buffer offset is `elapsed = compositionTime - compositionStart`
  off the same authoritative clock the HTMLMedia path drift-corrects toward, so the
  two land at the same content position within the strict-sync threshold. Worst
  case is a sub-tick discontinuity at the single transition instant — and as you
  said, strictly better than the pre-fix silence.

I can't do the ear-check myself, so I'm not adding speculative smoothing: a
one-sided gain ramp on the buffer would just trade a possible click for a ~5ms
dip (the element mute is instant). If a click is actually confirmed on a
slow-decode narration repro, the correct fix is a short **crossfade** — ramp the
element's volume down while ramping the buffer gain up, gated to the handoff path
— and I'll add that as a targeted follow-up.

Addressed the review feedback from Via and Rames:

**Container-vs-stream duration asymmetry** (both flagged this): the parity check now reads the audio stream's own `stream.duration` instead of `format.duration`. Added `streamDurationSeconds` to `AudioMetadata` (`ffprobe.ts`) — populated from `audioStream.duration`, falls back to `undefined` when the stream field is absent. The parity check prefers `streamDurationSeconds` over `durationSeconds`, falling back to container duration only when the stream field isn't available.

This closes the tautology risk where both sides collapse into `format.duration` on a broken mux.

All tests pass (ffprobe 14/14, parity 3/3, engine 79/79).

const frame = await player.captureFrame(time);

## Review — storyboard angle + live end-to-end testing

Reviewed the storyboard-facing surfaces statically, then **drove 6 workflows end-to-end on this branch** (`general-video`, `faceless-explainer`, `motion-graphics`, `pr-to-video`, `slideshow`, `website-to-video`) via a fresh `test-skills-fresh` sandbox — each rendered to a real 1080p30 MP4 and **verified from the encoded output** (ffmpeg frame extraction), plus a unit/parity pass on `subComposition` + the vendored parser.

### Verdict
The storyboard core is solid and the architecture is coherent, but driving real videos surfaced **3 blockers + a systemic validation gap** that would hit real users. Suggest fixing the blockers and the root-background/validation issues before merge; the rest are good follow-ups.

---

### 🔴 Blockers
- **B1 — `-refactor` skill names.** `faceless-explainer` and `pr-to-video` ship `name: …-refactor` in their SKILL.md frontmatter, so a real `npx skills add` installs them under `…-refactor/` and `/faceless-explainer` + `/pr-to-video` don't resolve — yet the router + 5–6 sibling skills route to those slugs. Drop the suffix (and grep for any other WIP names).
- **B2 — Silent/keyless runs dead-end at lint.** `build-frame` plants `caption-skin.html` at the project root; on a no-narration run nothing consumes it → `npx hyperframes lint` fails `multiple_root_compositions`, and the Step-6 gate hard-requires lint to pass. Confirmed independently on `faceless-explainer` and `pr-to-video`; undocumented. Fix: write/relocate the skin outside lint's root-discovery path on silent runs.
- **B3 — Slideshow renders only the first slide.** The SKILL's blessed authoring shape (sibling scene `<div data-composition-id>` with no master root) makes `render index.html` pick composition #1 and emit a truncated MP4 **with no warning** (e.g. 6s of a 40s deck). Fix: require a single master-root composition with slides as `class="clip"` children, and/or warn on multiple top-level comps + a slideshow island + no master.

### 🟠 Major
- **M1 — Root-background trap (invisible text).** A full-bleed background set on the **composition root** (the `data-composition-id` element) does **not** paint in the *assembled* render → dark text lands on the host `body{background:#000}` and is invisible. (The fixture avoids this by putting the fill on a child `.canvas`; a frame-worker output put it on the root → a launch-video frame rendered dark-ink-on-black.) The warning only lives in `frame-worker.md`, which the orchestrator-builds-frames path never forces you to read. Fix: require full-bleed backgrounds on a child clip and surface the rule in `SKILL.md`.
- **M2 — Validation doesn't reflect the assembled render (root of M1).** `validate`/WCAG/`snapshot` evaluate the *standalone* frame, so: (a) **false pass** — the root-bg trap passes WCAG + snapshot but ships invisible text; (b) **false fail** — WCAG computes contrast against the *page* background, not the actual child surface → ~100 bogus warnings on dark code surfaces. Only MP4 frame-extraction was ground truth. Fix: run contrast/layout checks against the composited output (or the element's real backdrop).
- **M3 — `assemble-index.mjs` exits 0 on a composition-id mismatch** while printing `✗ … id must match`, so a scripted pipeline proceeds on a non-assembled index. Fix: exit non-zero.

### 🟡 Minor / polish
- Crossfade transitions trip `inspect --strict-layout` `text_occluded` false-positives — the transition injector doesn't stamp `data-layout-allow-occlusion` on the wrappers it creates.
- `inspect` overflow ergonomics: suppression attrs must go on the clip/root (not the offending text), and the fix-hint misreports font-size (says "16px" for 560px text); also false `content_overlap` on stacked flex / number-lockups.
- `lint` rejects `-apple-system` in a font stack even with `system-ui`/`sans-serif` fallbacks.
- `lint` `gsap_studio_edit_blocked` advises "use CSS for initial visibility instead of `gsap.set()`" — conflicts with the required seek-safe `gsap.set(autoAlpha:0)` contract.
- `snapshot -o <dir>` is ignored (writes to project `snapshots/`); `snapshot` prints contradictory "fonts loaded" + "fonts FAILED [unloaded]".
- Render-summary duration is wrong (printed 20s for a 24s file) — cosmetic.
- `website-to-video` capture: `video-manifest.json` stores **DOM-display** dims (e.g. 904×613) not source res (1920×1080) → mis-scale risk if a planner sizes off it.
- `validate` missing from `hyperframes --help`; no documented slideshow→linear-MP4 path; `pr-to-video` registry copy claims `narrator_scripts.json`/`section_plan.md` but the skill is storyboard-based; `frame-worker.md` mandates `<template>`-wrapped roots but non-template frames pass all gates; the composition-id↔filename slug rule lives only in `frame-worker.md`.
- The storyboard parser is hand-vendored into 3 skills + core (4 copies), already whitespace-drifted, with no sync guard — consider a sync test or generate-from-core.

### 🟢 What's solid (verified)
- **`subComposition.ts`** — the 3 standalone-render fixes + 5 regression tests pass; storyboard posters render; the storyboard fixture renders correctly. Genuine improvement to the poster path.
- **`storyboard-format.md` / `script-format.md`** — accurate to the shipped `@hyperframes/core/storyboard` contract.
- **Vendored `storyboard.mjs` ↔ core parser** — byte-identical parse on the fixture (exact parity).
- **`contentExtractor.ts` capture change** — works as advertised: `[video]` clips surfaced first, well-formed `video-manifest.json`, correct caption fallback, files valid and render end-to-end.
- Architecture (router → workflow → domain skill) is coherent; the slideshow-island / hard-kill / font-face / seek-safe lint rules correctly enforce the contract. 6/6 workflows went prompt → rendered MP4 once authored correctly.

**On `pointer-events:none` and `interactive`**

`pointer-events:none` on `<hyperframes-player>` is intentional — it prevents stray clicks from toggling timeline playback while the presenter is navigating. When a composition needs interactive controls (native video controls, links, custom players), the `interactive` attribute opts out of this: it passes pointer events through to the composition iframe. So the inability to click video controls isn't a bug — it's the expected default, with `interactive` as the escape hatch.

**The media model (#1601)**

`ParentMediaManager` maintains mirror proxies of the iframe's `<audio>`/`<video>` elements in the parent frame. This matters because mobile browsers gate `el.play()` on user activation in the same frame — proxies in the parent frame inherit the user gesture from slideshow navigation. On every bridge tick (~80ms), `mirrorTime` syncs each proxy's `currentTime` to the timeline position.

The actual blocking happens inside the composition iframe's runtime. `syncRuntimeMedia` runs on every tick (~50ms) with `playing: false` when the slideshow holds, and enforces pause on any playing clip:

```ts
} else if (!params.playing && !el.paused) {
  el.pause();
}
```

`playSceneDocumentMedia`'s `play()` fires, then the runtime's next tick pauses it. `mirrorTime` in `ParentMediaManager` is a separate concern (parent-frame proxies) — the blocking is in the iframe runtime itself.

**Presenter → audience sync**

`wireSlideshowMedia` attaches native media event listeners (`play`, `pause`, `timeupdate`, `seeking`, `ended`, etc.) to every media element in the composition iframes. When the presenter's media fires one of these, `publishMediaState` broadcasts it over `BroadcastChannel('hf-slideshow:' + pathname)`. The audience window receives it via `onRemoteMedia`, which calls `applyRemoteMedia` — play events trigger `playAudienceMediaMuted` (starts muted first to comply with autoplay policy, then unlocks if permitted), pause/ended events pause directly. `timeupdate` is throttled to 450ms to avoid flooding the channel. This means autoplay on the presenter naturally propagates to the audience through the existing event-mirroring path — no extra wiring needed there.

**What's needed to make autoplay work**

The exemption needs to live in `syncRuntimeMedia` — a new control message from the player to the runtime flagging a specific clip as free-running, so `syncRuntimeMedia` skips the `!params.playing && !el.paused → pause()` enforcement for it. The player's `playSceneMedia` method sends this control, then calls `play()` on the clip. `stopMedia` on slide exit (already wired) sends the corresponding clear. The audience gets it through `wireSlideshowMedia` as normal — no extra work there.

The surface PR #1708 builds is exactly right — just needs that control message wired into the runtime.

**Authoring model question + skill guidance**

One thing worth clarifying before merge: how does `autoplay` get set, and when should it be used?

It's a static authoring decision — the composition author writes `"autoplay": true` on specific slides in the island JSON before handing the deck off. The presenter just navigates normally; slides marked autoplay start their video on enter. The slideshow still holds, presenter controls pacing with Next.

The default mental model should stay "presenter always initiates playback." `autoplay` is the narrow exception: slides where the video *is* the content (a recorded demo, a product walkthrough, a testimonial clip) and forcing a manual play click after navigating is just friction. The audience gets it automatically through the existing `wireSlideshowMedia` event-mirroring path — no extra wiring needed.

Without guidance in the slideshow skill, agents will add `autoplay: true` to every video slide by default — including background clips and anything the presenter talks over. Worth adding a short section before merge covering:

- **Use it when** the video is the primary content of the slide and its natural end is the cue to advance
- **Don't use it for** background/ambient video, clips the presenter talks over, or slides where the presenter might want to pause mid-video
- Audience sync is automatic through `wireSlideshowMedia`
- Leaving the slide always stops the clip (`stopMedia` is already wired on slide exit)

Really nice to see this land so fast — the push-then-read snapshot, the `--context-fields` slicing, the reuse of the selector-aware thumbnail route, and the type guards in `selection.ts` are all clean. Two things I'd flag after reading through, one substantive:

### 1. The published selection goes stale after an *external* edit — i.e. the agent flow this feature targets

The publisher effect in `useDomEditSession.ts` re-PUTs only when `domEditSelection` identity changes (deps `[domEditSelection, projectId]`). The only path that re-resolves `domEditSelection` against a reloaded DOM is `refreshDomEditSelectionFromPreview` (`useDomSelection.ts:371`), and its only callers are the studio's *own* commit hooks (`useDomEditCommits.ts`, `useDomEditTextCommits.ts`).

When an agent edits the composition file on disk, the flow is: file-change → `reloadPreview` → `setRefreshKey(k+1)` (`App.tsx:148`) → `NLELayout.tsx:152-161` does a *lightweight iframe `src` reload* ("instead of destroying the Player"). The React tree isn't remounted, so `useDomSelection` state persists. The `refreshKey` effect at `useDomSelection.ts:451` clears only the **hover**, not the selection. So:

- `domEditSelection` keeps the old (now-detached) element; its identity doesn't change → the publisher effect never fires → the server keeps serving the **previous** snapshot.
- If the agent removed/renamed the element, the stored `target.hfId` now points at nothing, but `GET /projects/:id/selection` (`selection.ts`) returns it verbatim with no staleness check — so `preview --context` reports a stale/invalid target as current.
- Even when the element survives a restyle, `boundingBox` / `computedStyles` / `textContent` stay frozen until the user re-clicks.

This is exactly the "select → agent edits → re-query" loop the feature is for, so it's worth closing. Options: re-run `refreshDomEditSelectionFromPreview` (or clear → publish `null`) on `refreshKey` change as well as on commits; and/or have the snapshot/`GET` carry a freshness signal the agent can check.

### 2. `--context` / `--selection` can't discover a Vite-served Studio (dev / local-studio modes) — silent `preview-not-running`

`findPreviewServerForProject` relies on `scanActiveServers`, which probes `/__hyperframes_config` over ports `3002..3101` (`MAX_PORT_SCAN=100`). But:

- The Vite-served studio (`runDevMode`, `runLocalStudioMode`) listens on **5190** (`packages/studio/vite.config.ts:187`) — outside the scan range.
- `/__hyperframes_config` is served only by the embedded CLI server (`cli/src/server/studioServer.ts:540`); `createStudioApi` doesn't register it.

So in those modes the studio *does* publish selections (the Vite plugin mounts `createStudioApi` under `/api/`), but the CLI can't find the server and returns `preview-not-running` — even though the skill tells the agent to run `preview --context` unconditionally.

End users via `npx hyperframes init` + `preview` are unaffected (no template depends on `@hyperframes/studio`, so they hit embedded mode, which is discoverable). It mainly bites contributors and anyone with `@hyperframes/studio` installed locally — and it fails silently. A line in the skill, or exposing `/__hyperframes_config` from the Vite plugin (+ tolerating the 5190 port), would cover it.

The per-frame fixes are in #1775. The main findings were:

1. **WAAPI adapter scan on every seek.** In `v0.7.5`, `renderSeek` called the WAAPI adapter once per frame, and that adapter called `document.getAnimations()` every time, even for GSAP-only compositions where it returned `[]`. That was a real Chromium per-frame tax. `0.7.18` skips the global scan after empty discovery and tracks late-created WAAPI animations lazily.

2. **CSS adapter scan on every seek.** In `v0.7.5`, CSS animation handling called `el.getAnimations()` per tracked element per seek. `0.7.18` caches discovered CSS animation handles during adapter discovery instead of re-querying Chromium every frame.

3. **CPU/Linux GPU auto-detection.** In `v0.7.5`, `browserGpuMode=auto` only checked whether WebGL context creation succeeded. Hi Miguel‚ I think I found the per-frame regression in source. Pinpoint + numbers below.

Root cause (confirmed in v0.7.5 source):
packages/producer/src/services/renderOrchestrator.ts:1216 (and distributed/renderChunk.ts:510):
    captureBeyondViewport: composition.videos.length > 0
For any composition with video, 0.7.x sets captureBeyondViewport: true on the per-frame Page.captureScreenshot, which moves capture onto Chrome's beyond-viewport compositor (full-surface re-composite per frame). That's cheap on a GPU but brutal under software rasterization (SwiftShader) ‚ which is the default headless-Linux server path. True 0.6.42 had captureBeyondViewport=false everywhere (fast). #1094 turned it on for all paths; #1670 restored the fast default only for the non-video opaque case and left video compositions on the slow path, with NO hardware-vs-software gate.

Why it only shows on servers: on a GPU the beyond-viewport compositor is nearly free; on CPU-only SwiftShader (standard headless render hosts) it re-rasterizes the full surface every frame and scales with composition complexity. That's why it's invisible on GPU dev machines and ~5x on our render nodes.

Measured (same staging host, AWS c6a.4xlarge, software render; identical config; only the producer image swapped; wall render time per composition):

| Composition         | 0.6.42 | 0.7.5  | 0.7.18 |
|---------------------|--------|--------|--------|
| A (light overlay)   | 13.2s  | 30.4s  | 24.5s  |
| B (medium, list)    | 10.3s  | 53.0s  | 45.7s  |
| C (heavy, b-roll)   | 11.2s  | 64.0s  | 55.8s  |
| D (heavy, scroll b-roll) | 11.1s | 96.0s | 96.8s |

Full-suite 0.7.18 = 51.5s mean over 39/39 (2 timeouts). Stage timing pins it to per-frame capture (captureFrameMs ‚ 45‚61s on heavy comps; compile <1s, browser-probe ~1ms). The video-containing compositions regress hardest, consistent with the captureBeyondViewport gate above.

Proposed fix: don't force the beyond-viewport path under software rendering. e.g. gate the opt-in on hardware acceleration ‚
    captureBeyondViewport: composition.videos.length > 0 && browserGpuMode === "hardware"
(or expose it as config / default-off under software). The original #1094 motivation (portrait video edge-clip under multi-tab load) needs preserving for the GPU path, but a 5x software regression on every video render is the bigger cost. There may also be a smaller secondary cost on non-video comps (dedup-verification arming) worth a look, but the gate above is the dominant fix.

The prior `setSvg()` only moved the sink (`innerHTML` → `DOMParser` + `importNode`); it did **not** sanitize, so active SVG content still executed on insertion. I reproduced your finding and then verified the fix in headless Chrome (same helper, both templates):

| | old `setSvg` (importNode-only) | new `setSvg` (sanitizing) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fired handlers | `["script","onload"]` | `[]` |
| trusted icon renders | — | ✅ `svg>path` present |
| danger nodes in output | — | `0` |
| `on*` attrs in output | — | `0` |

`setSvg()` now runs a **default-deny** `cleanSvg()` over the parsed tree before it touches the document: only an allow-list of inert drawing elements (`svg/g/path/line/rect/circle/ellipse/defs/linearGradient/stop/text/…`) and presentation attributes (`d/fill/stroke/viewBox/transform/…`) survives. Everything else — `<script>`, `<image>`, `<use>`, `<foreignObject>`, `<a>`, `<animate>`, **every `on*` handler**, and `href`/`xlink:href`/`style` — is stripped, including on the root node. - **Superset row is byte-identical to main** (`fd07cd22e945` from both builds): slicing the union window produces exactly the frames per-trim extraction produced, while decoding the source once instead of four times. Wall-clock gain on a 14-core box is modest (1.26x — main's four extractions ran in parallel; the union is one process) but CPU work halves, so the gain grows on core-constrained runners (Lambda) and the keyframe seek cost is paid once instead of per trim. Disjoint or non-frame-aligned trims keep the direct path; a union failure falls back to per-trim extraction, so superset can't introduce a new failure mode.
- **VFR note**: a VFR source whose trims superset can pick a one-frame-adjacent held frame at irregular-timestamp tie points vs the old per-trim extraction (both picks are valid for the same sample time; frame counts and sample times are unchanged, verified by the mid-seek content check landing on the exact source timestamp).
- **Cache-key correctness fix** found while making trims smart: the HDR preflight rewrote `videoPath` AFTER the cache-key snapshot, so a mixed-HDR render cached BT.2020-converted frames under the plain source key — a later SDR render of the same trim would have served HDR-tinted frames. Latent while the cache was opt-in; real once commit 2 defaulted it on. The key now carries a transform discriminator (absent = byte-compatible with existing entries), pinned by tests.
- **One-pass SDR→HDR**: same shape as the VFR fix — the libx264 pre-encode is gone, the `colorspace` remap runs inside the extraction pass.

- **Hardcoded fixture values / i18n-fragile h3 selectors**: sections are now found via a new `data-panel-section` attribute on the `Section` primitive (one-line, zero-risk addition) instead of matching `h3.textContent` + a manual tree walk. Individual fields are found by their sibling label text (or, where a field has no label, by being the section's only input of that type) instead of by guessing the fixture's current value ahead of time.
- **sleep(1400/2000/6000)**: replaced with polling on the actual condition (selection registered, section rendered, patch round-tripped, app booted).
- **No `__patchLog` dump on FAIL**: `check()` now dumps it on any failure.
- **No fault-injection cell**: added one — the server rejects a patch and the panel must toast the rejection without persisting it or clobbering the prior committed value.

**Bugs the actual run surfaced** (worth noting since "never run with agent-browser" was itself one of the findings — turns out that's why these were invisible):
1. The *original* script only silently passed 7/10 checks even before my changes — `#qa-shape` selection was landing back on the headline, which masked two downstream checks into false positives (`opacity`/`radius` "passed" by matching a substring anywhere in the file, not confirming the right element changed).
2. Root cause: computing click coordinates immediately after a commit reused a stale preview-frame position from before the property panel's layout reflow (opening/resizing the panel shifts the iframe's on-page position). Fixed by waiting for two consecutive reads of the frame's rect to agree before trusting it.
3. A real disk-write race on the very first commit of a run: the patch fetch resolving client-side doesn't guarantee the server's file write has landed. Fixed with a short bounded poll on disk content instead of asserting immediately.

Verified: 14/14 checks pass across repeated clean runs (fresh fixture copy + fresh preview server each time).

Correction to the suggested fix: `build-zip.ts` already has a `banner` on the handler bundle (the `createRequire` shim for `require`) — so the fix is to **extend that existing banner** with the `__filename`/`__dirname` lines rather than add a new `banner` key (a duplicate key is silently overridden, which cost us a deploy cycle):

```ts
banner: {
  js: [
    "// hyperframes-aws-lambda handler bundle",
    'import { createRequire as __hf_createRequire } from "module";',
    "const require = __hf_createRequire(import.meta.url);",
    'import { fileURLToPath as __hf_fileURLToPath } from "url";',
    'import { dirname as __hf_dirname } from "path";',
    "const __filename = __hf_fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);",
    "const __dirname = __hf_dirname(__filename);",
  ].join("\n"),
},
```

Will confirm against a live stack shortly and report back.

Confirmed on a live stack: with the existing banner extended as above, the same render that failed at import now completes — 180/180 frames, 6s 1080x1920@30 composition, $0.0067. The banner extension is the complete fix; no sidecar staging needed (wawoff2 embeds its wasm as a data URI).
